sections.h2: Ways to sell a Prior Lake house
sections.html:
A Prior Lake owner can go to market with an agent, handle the sale alone, or sell directly to a home-buying company. Which one makes sense usually comes down to condition, timing and whether the house sits on the water.

The city lies about 20 miles southwest of Minneapolis in Scott County, beside Savage and Shakopee, and State Highway 13 makes the commute easy. A well-kept house on a street near the lakes usually does fine on the open market. A house with a failing roof, an estate attached or a tenant who will not leave tends to suit a direct sale, where the buyer accepts the property in its present state and you pick the closing day.

  • Listing with an agent: broad reach, but you prepare the house and wait for a buyer's lender.
  • Selling it yourself: you keep the commission and take on the contract work.
  • Direct sale: little prep, a quick closing, and an offer that accounts for repairs.

sections.h2: Prior Lake owners and housing costs
sections.html:
Prior Lake is a family-and-owner city. About 86 of every 100 homes are lived in by the people who own them, and the typical household has 2.79 people. The estimated population reached 28,140 on July 1, 2025, up 1.9% from 27,616 in 2020.

Households earned a median of $134,255 over 2020 to 2024. Owners put the middle home's worth at $450,700, and renters paid a median of $1,654. Some 91% of residents were in the same home a year earlier, so most owners have been in place a while.

sections.h2: Short-term rental limits and your sale
sections.html:
Prior Lake permits only rentals of at least 60 days and no more than 180 days in its residential districts. Rentals shorter than 60 days are prohibited there, and a permit with a $250 application fee is required for the permitted range.

The rules live in City Code Sections 4-380 through 4-388. A permit expires each December 31 and cannot move to a new owner or a different dwelling, so a buyer of your house cannot inherit it. A named local agent who lives and works within 30 miles has to answer calls around the clock while the home is rented, and the dwelling must have off-street parking equal to the number of bedrooms. At most two restricted watercraft may be moored at the property. The ordinance caps overnight guests by lot size and floor area:

Overnight occupant limits for Prior Lake short-term rentals (City Code 4-384)
Lot sizeMain building under 1,500 sq ft1,500 to under 2,000 sq ft2,000 sq ft or more
One-half acre or more6812
Under one-half acre468

Children under three do not count toward these totals. A seller with a tenant under lease should pass along the lease and the permit file, and explain that the permit ends with the seller's ownership.

sections.h2: City rules that can trip up a seller
sections.html:
The Code Enforcement Division enforces a long list of ordinances, and several of them come up while a house is being readied for the market. Fixing these items before a buyer's inspection saves you from last-minute credits.

  • Grass and weeds: growth taller than 12 inches is unlawful during the April 1 to November 1 growing season.
  • Snow on sidewalks: owners must clear public sidewalks within 48 hours after a snowfall ends.
  • Junk vehicles and debris: unlicensed or inoperable vehicles must be inside a building, and piles of boards or tires count as nuisances.
  • Recreational equipment: winter equipment may sit by the driveway from November 1 to April 1, and summer equipment from April to November 1, if it has current plates and runs.
  • Driveways and decks: replacing or widening a driveway takes a permit, and structures need a building permit.

Work near the shore carries lower limits. Moving more than 10 cubic yards of material, or disturbing more than 500 square feet, on steep slopes or in the bluff, shore impact or shoreland zones needs approval, while the threshold elsewhere is 50 cubic yards. A person who skips a required permit and applies afterward pays double the stated fee. Call Code Enforcement at 952-447-9811 before you start any project you plan to disclose or finish ahead of a sale.

Prior Lake takes its name from two connected lakes, Lower Prior Lake at about 810 acres and Upper Prior Lake at about 354, linked by a navigable channel under Eagle Creek Avenue. Spring Lake, 290 acres, lies partly within the city along Scott County Road 12. The water is the reason many buyers look here.

Lakefront and lake-access homes are priced as a separate market from interior streets. Zebra mussels were confirmed in both the lower and the upper lake, so lake-property buyers sometimes ask about docks, lifts and invasive species. Have your dock and lift details ready, along with any permits you hold for shore work.

sections.h2: What Scott County requires when a house closes
sections.html:
Scott County's Land Records Department records deeds, mortgages, assignments, releases and satisfactions. It reviews each document for recordable form, but its staff cannot supply legal forms or advice, so use your title company or an attorney.

Under Minnesota Statutes section 513.55, you hand the buyer a signed statement of known defects ahead of the purchase agreement. Section 103I.235 adds a well statement on or with the deed. Sales above $3,000 also need a value certificate filed with the county, and the county and state websites list the deed tax rate and recording fees.

Scott County offers a free Property Watch alert that emails you whenever a document is recorded under your name and parcel number. Sign up before you sell if you want a record of when the deed lands.

A typical order of work: finish any permitted repairs, write the defect statement, check for wells, and let the title company file the value certificate and deed. Ask for the final settlement statement and compare it with your offer before you sign, and keep a copy of the recorded deed afterward.

The county assessor values each parcel as of January 2 and mails a notice each March. Sales that are not arm's length, such as bank sales, short sales, foreclosures, auctions and transfers between relatives, are left out of its sales analysis. Appraisers walk about 11,000 parcels a year, so every property is viewed at least once every five years. The second half of the property tax is due October 15, so confirm it was paid before you close.

faqs.q: Can I rent my Prior Lake house by the weekend?
faqs.a: No. Prior Lake prohibits rentals shorter than 60 days in every residential district. The city permits stays of 60 to 180 days with a permit and a $250 fee.

faqs.q: Does a short-term rental permit transfer to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. The permit cannot be transferred to another person or another dwelling, and it expires each December 31. A buyer who wants to rent the house must apply separately.

faqs.q: Which pre-sale fixes in Prior Lake need a city permit?
faqs.a: Building work, driveway replacement or widening, and some grading near the shore all need city permits. Starting without one means applying afterward at double the fee.

faqs.q: Where does a Prior Lake deed get recorded?
faqs.a: The Scott County Land Records Department does. Your title company normally handles the filing.

faqs.q: What is the sidewalk snow deadline in Prior Lake?
faqs.a: Forty-eight hours after the snowfall ends. Do not push snow into the street. Keep the walk clear while the house is listed, because showings continue all winter.
